newsitem.title: USA: U.S. body fines German for campaign donations. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: U.S. body fines German for campaign donations. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: The U.S. Federal Election Commission said on Friday it had fined a German businessman, Thomas Kramer, a record $323,000 for numerous illegal political contribitions.

Kramer agreed to pay the fine, the largest ever levied against an individual by the FEC, to settle the case. He said through his lawyer he was unaware that it was illegal for foreign citizens to give money to U.S. political candidates.
The FEC also fined the Republican Party of Florida $82,000 for its role in the affair.

The case comes at a time when a Senate committee is holding hearings into illegal foreign contributions to the Democratic Party during the 1996 election campaign. Kramer's activities took place in 1993-94.

According to a conciliation agreement signed by Kramer and the general counsel of the FEC, Kramer acknowledged making contributions to various local, state and federal political committees both in his own name, in the name of his secretary and through the 17 Florida-based companies he controlled, most of which were involved in tourism development projects.

He made a direct contribution of $95,000 to the Republican Party and asked his secretary, Terri Bradley, to made contributions of an additional $21,000 in his name, for which he subsequently reimbursed her.
Not only is it illegal for foreigners to make political contributions, it is illegal for anybody to give donations in the name of another person.
Kramer's many donations to various candidates made through his corporations totalled $287,600. In all, Kramer's contributions through myriad sources came to $322,600.

Though Republicans appear to have been the main beneficiaries of Kramer's largesse, Democrats also received some donations, among them the Democratic National Committee, Nebraska (corrects from Nevada) Sen. Bob Kerrey and former Maine Sen. George Mitchell.
The FEC did not say how much these and other individual candidates received.

The FEC sent admonishment letters to a long list of candidates but took no further action against them. However, the agency asked the national committees of both parties to return any funds they had received from Kramer.
The case is likely to give ammunition to Democrats who have arged that they were not alone in receiving foreign money and that Republicans were also guilty.
The Democratic National Committee has returned more than $3 million raised illegally, much of it from Asian individuals or companies. The Republicans have returned $122,000.
At the centre of the Senate investigation is former Democratic fund raiser John Huang, who used his wide contacts to Asian business interests to raise millions of dollars.
